review_notes: I read all 558 lines of the target file and checked the declarations it depends on and the files that use it or contain similar material: AbsoluteIrreducibilityBaseChange.lean (nullstellensatz descent, `irreducible_map_of_irreducible_map_algebraicClosure`, `irreducible_map_perfectConstantsToFrobeniusSubfield`), PerfectConstants.lean (`perfectConstantsToFrobeniusSubfield`, its `coe` lemma and injectivity), PlaneCurveBidegreeBridge.lean (which already contains `irreducible_of_irreducible_map_algebraicClosure`), SeparatingCoordinateNotFrobenius.lean, and PoweredCoordinates.lean (downstream user of `minpoly_natDegree_over_frobeniusSubfield_eq_char`). The remaining repetitions in the target — the three `@[simp]` generator lemmas of `planeCurveToBivariate` (lines 50–99), the two bidegree theorems closing with `degreeOf_map_eq_of_injective` and injectivity of the constant map (lines 194–215), the three `ringHom_ext`/`fin_cases` comparisons (117–132, 148–169, 224–256), and the `IsDomain`/`CharP` instance plumbing — are short calculations, routine unfolding or instance boilerplate, so I did not report them under this rubric. The single finding is the fourfold repetition, including statement/proof duplication inside the same declaration, of the absolute-irreducibility-to-irreducibility descent, for which a named lemma already exists elsewhere in the repository. I could not compile any proposed replacement; the claim that the revised `let hf` terms stay definitionally identical is argued from the syntax, not tested.

findings.problem: Both absolute-irreducibility theorems derive `Irreducible f` from `habsolute` with the same four-line term, and they do so twice each: once in the statement, where it is needed to install `planeCurveCoordinateRing_isDomain hf` under `letI`, and once verbatim in the proof (lines 464-467 and 484-487 in the first theorem; lines 514-517 and 532-535 in the second). The duplicated reasoning is the algebraic-closure descent step supplied by `irreducible_map_of_irreducible_map_algebraicClosure` at `RingHom.id K` followed by `MvPolynomial.map_id`. The repository already packages exactly this result as `irreducible_of_irreducible_map_algebraicClosure` in `PlaneCurveBidegreeBridge.lean` (lines 53-61), but that file is not imported here, so the target recomputes it in four places. This is also brittle for maintenance: the `dsimp only` at lines 493 and 541 only exposes the intended forall-type if the statement-level and proof-level `let hf` denote the same term, so any edit to one copy (for instance changing the `simpa` set) silently disconnects the proof from the statement context.
findings.proposed_change:
Move `irreducible_of_irreducible_map_algebraicClosure` into `AbsoluteIrreducibilityBaseChange.lean` immediately after `irreducible_map_of_irreducible_map_algebraicClosure` (so it is in the import closure of this file without importing the whole bidegree bridge), with the statement

```
theorem irreducible_of_irreducible_map_algebraicClosure
    {K : Type*} [Field K] {f : MvPolynomial (Fin 2) K}
    (habsolute : Irreducible (MvPolynomial.map (algebraMap K (AlgebraicClosure K)) f)) :
    Irreducible f := by
  have h := irreducible_map_of_irreducible_map_algebraicClosure
    (RingHom.id K) f habsolute
  rwa [MvPolynomial.map_id] at h
```

(proof sketch: the nullstellensatz descent lemma applied to the identity embedding, with `MvPolynomial.map_id` rewriting the constant extension out). Then replace each of the four occurrences by the single line

```
    let hf : Irreducible f := irreducible_of_irreducible_map_algebraicClosure habsolute
```

in the statement (as in lines 464-467 and 514-517) and by the analogous line in the proof (lines 484-487 and 532-535); both occurrences are then literally the same closed term, which is what the subsequent `dsimp only` step needs. The same replacement can be applied at the already-duplicated uses in `PlaneCurveBidegreeBridge.lean` (lines 72, 75, 91, 94).
findings.benefit: The descent from absolute irreducibility to irreducibility over `K` becomes one named, reusable fact with a single proof, instead of a repeated `simpa`-wrapped application; the two long theorem statements lose four lines each and the two proofs lose four lines each, and a reader immediately sees which hypothesis creates the `IsDomain (PlaneCurveCoordinateRing f)` instance. Keeping the statement-level and proof-level `let` syntactically identical also removes the hidden coupling to `dsimp only`, so future changes to the descent proof cannot break the statement/proof match.

theorem irreducible_of_irreducible_map_algebraicClosure
    {f : MvPolynomial (Fin 2) K}
    (habsolute : Irreducible
      (MvPolynomial.map (algebraMap K (AlgebraicClosure K)) f)) :
    Irreducible f := by
  have h := irreducible_map_of_irreducible_map_algebraicClosure
    (RingHom.id K) f habsolute
  rw [MvPolynomial.map_id] at h

theorem irreducible_map_of_irreducible_map_algebraicClosure
    {K F σ : Type*} [Field K] [Field F]
    (iF : K →+* F) (f : MvPolynomial σ K)
    (habsolute : Irreducible
      (MvPolynomial.map (algebraMap K (AlgebraicClosure K)) f)) :
    Irreducible (MvPolynomial.map iF f)
